learningPurpose: Prepare students to describe pressure as normal force per area, predict the effect of changing either input, and calculate an introductory result using consistent SI units.

definitions.meaning: Force distributed over an area in a fluid or on a surface.

governingPrinciples: Pressure calculations require consistent force and area units.
This file covers introductory static-pressure reasoning only.

sourceReferences.section: Introduction to Pressure in Fluid Mechanics

assumptions: The force is applied normally over the stated area.
The example is educational and not a pressure-vessel design case.
limitations: Does not cover fluid dynamics, leakage, compressibility, component losses, transient response, pressure-vessel design, or equipment ratings.
The force arrow, contact-area geometry, and pressure intensity are representational and not dimensioned physical models.
The cited web edition has no fixed page numbering.

workedExample.title: Pressure from a known force and area
workedExample.purpose: Show the required SI-unit relationship without creating a full lesson.
steps: Check that force and area are in SI units.
Divide force by area to obtain pressure in pascals.
workedExample.answer: The result is 100,000 Pa, or 100 kPa for display.

normalOperation: A valid normal-force input and positive area input produce a pressure result through EQ-FLUID-PRESSURE-001.
commonMisconceptions: Treating pressure and force as the same quantity.
Entering an area in cm^2 or mm^2 as if it were m^2.
Treating an ideal classroom result as an equipment rating.
